title: Pathogens
examples: What is the difference between bacteria and viruses?
How do these germs actually make us sick?
Can we stop the spread of these pathogens?

explain.say: Today we are learning about pathogens. Pathogens are tiny living things that can cause sickness. We will learn about four main types of these pathogens.

items: We must learn to prevent them

explain.say: First we look at bacteria. Bacteria are single-celled living organisms. They reproduce very quickly through simple division. A common example is the bacteria that causes strep throat.
Next we study viruses. Viruses are much smaller than bacteria. They need a living host cell to reproduce themselves. A common example is the virus that causes the common cold.
Then there are fungi. Fungi are often seen as molds or yeasts. They can cause infections like athlete's foot. These organisms are not plants or animals.
Finally we look at protists. Protists are diverse single-celled eukaryotes. A common example is the protozoan that causes malaria. They are quite varied in their structure.
Pathogens spread through various ways. Direct contact, like touching someone with a rash, is one way. Another way is through contaminated food or water.

faq.a: Viruses are often described as being on the border of life. They cannot reproduce on their own and need a host cell to do so. You might also ask if they are really alive or how they multiply.

faq.q: What is the main difference between bacteria and viruses?
faq.a: Bacteria are single-celled organisms that can reproduce independently. Viruses are much smaller and must hijack a living cell to multiply. You could also ask if bacteria need a host or what makes them different.
asks: Does a virus need a cell to live?

faq.q: How do we stop pathogens from spreading?
faq.a: We can stop spread through good hygiene practices. Washing hands frequently and keeping surfaces clean are very effective methods. Another way to ask is what are prevention methods or how do we stop germ spread?
No, many bacteria are harmless and even helpful. For example, some live in our gut and help us digest food. You might ask if all germs are bad or are there good bacteria?

faq.q: What is the difference between fungi and protists?
faq.a: Fungi are a kingdom of organisms, like molds, that get nutrients from decay. Protists are a very diverse group of single-celled eukaryotes that don't fit elsewhere. You could ask what kind of organisms fungi are or what protists are.

facts: Bacteria can reproduce asexually by binary fission.
Viruses use the host cell's machinery to replicate.
Fungi include yeasts, molds, and mushrooms.
Protists are a varied group including amoebas and paramecia.

quiz.say: Which pathogen group is described as needing a living host cell to reproduce?
quiz.why: Viruses are obligate intracellular parasites, meaning they must invade a host cell to replicate their genetic material.

wrong.0: Fungi obtain nutrients through absorption, not by hijacking a host cell's machinery.
wrong.1: Protists are self-sufficient single-celled organisms, though they are diverse.
wrong.3: Bacteria can reproduce independently using their own cell division processes.

quiz.say: If you touch a surface contaminated by a pathogen, what is the most direct way the pathogen might enter your body?
quiz.show: Direct contact is a major route.
quiz.why: Direct contact involves physical transfer from a contaminated source to your skin or mucous membranes.

wrong.1: Ingestion is swallowing the pathogen, which is a different route than touching.
wrong.2: Inhalation involves breathing the pathogen in, which is only one specific way of spread.
wrong.3: Vector transmission requires an intermediate carrier like a mosquito, which is a specific type of spread.

quiz.say: Which group includes organisms like athlete's foot fungus?
quiz.why: Athlete's foot is a common fungal infection, belonging to the group of fungi.

wrong.0: Bacteria cause infections like strep throat, not typically skin molds.
wrong.1: Viruses cause illnesses like the cold, not usually fungal skin infections.
wrong.2: Protists are generally single-celled organisms, unlike the filamentous nature of mold.
